word.name: field-mark-allowed
word.title: Field Mark Allowed
word.description: A field marked to be carried on its elements' Neo4j nodes is a plain top-level field of a concept, with a property node in the concept's property tree, and a property name that no other mark yields and that nothing else wrote.

graphRule.name: field-mark-allowed
graphRule.says: a field marked to be carried on its elements' Neo4j nodes is a plain top-level field of a concept, with a property node in the concept's property tree, and a property name that no other mark yields and that nothing else wrote. A mark is one `HAS_ELEMENT` edge from the set of neo4j properties that are also fields, `39999:<TA>:the-set-of-neo4j-properties-that-are-also-fields`, to the field's property node. It makes each current element of the concept carry the field's value from its JSON, as a node property.
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about the owner's and the admins' own marks (D4). Every element of the set counts as a mark, whoever made the edge.
graphRule.check: the same `violations` over every current mark names each mark whose field has changed type, lost its property node, or now collides. `rules check` (A10.31) will run it over the graph.
graphRule.repair: `graph unmark-field` takes a broken mark out, with its copies; `graph map-fields` brings a concept's copies in line with its marks.
graphRule.enforcedBy: the guard of `graph mark-field`. The rule's code is in `src/operations/rules/field-mark-allowed.js`, and the mapping it guards is in `src/operations/catalog/graph/_fields.js`. Built in story graph-operations-foundation #5 (ADR 0005).

alsoSays.label: The naming convention
alsoSays.text: a marked field's property is `<key>_<field>`, the concept's key (its `oKeys.singular`) and the field's name joined by `_`, such as `dog_breed` for Dog's `breed`. The name is computed every time, never stored, and one mark yields it across the graph. Names starting `<key>_` on an element of a concept with that key belong to marks: `graph map-fields` removes one that no mark yields, such as a copy left by a field that has left the schema.

code.summary: A field marked to be carried on its elements' Neo4j nodes is a plain top-level field of a concept, with a property node in its property tree, and a property name no other mark yields and nothing else wrote.

refusals.when: The graph has no concept for neo4j properties, or no set of neo4j properties that are also fields: install the firmware first
A concept that names no concept header: a node labelled ConceptHeader, or ListHeader for one the nostr import brought in
A field that isn't one of the concept's top-level fields, jsonSchema.properties[<concept key>].properties

The field has no property node under its concept's section node in the concept's property tree, or the concept has no primary property: give the concept's fields their nodes first with graph set-schema or another property write, which sign nothing, or POST /api/normalize/generate-property-tree, which signs
The field holds an object, a list of objects or a list of lists, which no Neo4j property can hold
The concept's key isn't letters and digits, so <key>_<field> can't be written unquoted in Cypher
Another mark already yields the same property name: another concept with the same key marked a field of the same name
A current element of the concept already carries the property name, though the field isn't marked: something else wrote it
